texts: Please write a doha about the fakir who walks the roads owning nothing at all and so has nothing that a tax collector or a king could ever take from him, and sleeps without any fear.
My college friend left a salaried job to live on almost nothing, and I have never seen anyone so unafraid of tomorrow.
Who owns nothing fears nothing; the king trembles on his seat while the fakir laughs at the wind.
doha about the freedom of having nothing to lose
owning nothing, fearing nothing
I want a doha about a wandering holy man who gave up every possession on purpose, who is richer in freedom than the wealthy, and who walks into any town without worry about what could be lost.
When burglars hit our street, the only home they left alone belonged to the old fakir who had nothing and sat on his step smiling.
fakir's freedom
Naked of possessions, light of heart, the fakir goes where he pleases, for nothing holds him back.
write a doha on giving up everything to be free
doha about a fakir who sees himself in a mirror and sees someone who owns nothing and fears nothing
mirror, fakir, fearless
The fakir looks into the mirror and sees only a face without need, and a heart without fear.
My uncle gave away his mirror, his watch, and his shiny things last year, and says he finally looks at himself without worry.
Write a doha where a fakir looks into a mirror and finds nothing to hide, nothing to polish, nothing to lose, and declares himself the freest of men because he chose to own nothing.
My cousin burned through his savings chasing a get-rich scheme, and my aunt who owns nothing just laughed and said, the philosopher's stone is owning nothing and fearing nothing.
doha with philosopher's stone, how the wandering saint with nothing is richer than a rich man
philosopher's stone, owning nothing

Please write a doha where the fakir refuses the philosopher's stone that could turn all to wealth, because he knows that owning nothing brings a freedom no wealth can match, and a fear that no robber can arouse.
The philosopher's stone is offered to the fakir, and he smiles, for he who owns nothing has already found the greater treasure.
potter, clay, rainbird, nothing owned
The potter in our lane gave his whole shop to his son, took nothing but his clay-stained clothes, and now sits happily listening for the rainbird.
Write a doha about a fakir who owns neither clay nor wheel nor the potter's trade, who listens for the rainbird and sleeps wherever evening finds him, free because there is nothing left to lose.
The potter's clay is broken and forgotten, the rainbird calls, and the fakir who owns nothing is afraid of nothing.
doha with a potter and clay and a rainbird, about the freedom of owning nothing
Light is the one who has set down every burden, and the road welcomes him like a friend.
doha about choosing to live with nothing and being totally fearless

Please write a doha for someone who has given away everything they owned of their own free will and discovered that having nothing means there is nothing to protect, nothing to fear and nothing to lose.
After I sold everything and moved into a rented room with a single bag, I slept better than I had in ten years.
nothing owned, nothing feared
In my uncle's village, every home has a heavy lock except the fakir's hut, which stands open, and he has never once been robbed or afraid.
doha with a lock, about a fakir who needs no lock because he owns nothing
lock, nothing to guard
No lock hangs on the fakir's hut, for what is there to keep, and what is there to fear?
Write a doha where the rich man fits a heavy lock to guard his goods while the fakir has nothing to lock away, so that the poor man alone sleeps in freedom and without worry.
fish, fakir's freedom
A fish in the water owns nothing, carries nothing, and fears no robber, and the fakir who has chosen to own nothing lives the same carefree life; please write a doha on that.
doha with a fish, about a fakir who owns nothing and has no fear
The fish owns no pond, the fakir owns no roof, and both drift free wherever life takes them.
Watching a fish dart through the shallows I thought of my friend who gave up his home and job and now travels freely with a single bag.
furnace, fakir, fearless
The furnace roars for the rich man's gain, while the fakir warms himself with his own freedom and fears no ending.
Write a doha where a furnace burns day and night for a merchant counting his profits, and a fakir passes by with empty hands, free from every worry that profit brings to the owner.
doha with a furnace, about the fakir who owns nothing and so fears nothing
The owner of the foundry down the road works the furnace around the clock to protect his business, while a wandering holy man sleeps soundly outside his gate.
He who has thrown away his bundle of wants walks on, singing, with all the sky for his roof.

I'd like a doha that celebrates the person who chose to live with nothing, who has no savings to lose, no property to defend, and no reputation to guard, and who therefore walks through the world without a tremble.
owning nothing, free
doha on a fakir who gave up everything and is happy
My neighbour gave away his flat, his car and his bank account, and when I asked if he was afraid, he said there was nothing left to be afraid for.
The touchstone tests the wares of the merchant and finds some of it false, but it cannot test the fakir, who owns nothing and so has nothing that could be found wanting. Please write a doha on that.
When the banker's investments were tested by the crash, he lost sleep for weeks, and the wandering saint at his gate, who owned nothing, was not troubled at all.
The touchstone can test the trader's treasure, but what can it test in the fakir, who carries nothing and fears nothing?
doha with a touchstone, about the fakir who owns nothing
touchstone, nothing to test
Poor in possessions, rich in being, the fakir walks the world as a king walks his garden.
choosing to own nothing

Please write a doha about the quiet pride of the one who chose to be without, who needs no one's permission, fears no one's anger and lacks no one's approval, because there is nothing anyone can take.
doha on the freedom of the mendicant who owns nothing
My grandmother gave her last ornaments to the shrine and then said, now I can finally go anywhere without worry.
When we were robbed on a train, the saintly old man in our compartment, who carried only a cloth bag, was the one who sat completely calm; I want a doha on him.
Please compose a doha about a wandering faqir who has nothing to be robbed of, nothing to be proud of and nothing to be afraid of, and who therefore feels richer than a rich man travelling in fear.
The robber leaves the fakir untouched, for what does he have to steal from one who has chosen to have nothing?
fakir, empty-handed, fearless
doha on how having nothing means no fear
A rope binds the cattle of the rich man, the buckets of the village, the chests of the merchant, and the fakir owns no rope because he is bound to nothing. Write a doha about his freedom.
Our village headman is tied by a hundred ropes of obligation to his land, while the wandering fakir who passes through each winter is tied to nothing and smiles at everything.
Every rope of ownership ties a man to the earth, and the fakir has cut them all and walks as light as air.
rope, unbound fakir
doha with a rope, about a fakir who owns nothing so nothing ties him down
The salt of the sea is the weaver's wage, yet the fakir wants neither salt nor cloth, and that is his wealth.
salt, loom, owning nothing
doha with salt and a weaver's loom, a fakir who gave up everything
Write a doha where a weaver at his loom works for a pinch of salt and a day's cloth, while a fakir who has chosen to own neither passes by, freer than both the weaver and the trader.
My friend sold his loom and his small salt business to wander on the road, saying he would rather own nothing and fear nothing.
The fakir rests a night at the inn with a small lamp, and by morning he has left without a single thing behind.
Please write a doha about a fakir who stays a night at an inn, has no possessions to unpack, lights a little lamp for company, and leaves at dawn with nothing lost, as free and fearless as ever.
At a small inn on my trip, the only guest who slept deeply was the old fakir by the lamp, who had nothing to guard and nothing to pack.
doha with an inn and a lamp, about a fakir who owns nothing
inn, lamp, nothing owned
doha with fire and a moneylender, about a fakir who owns nothing and fears nothing
When fire consumes the moneylender's ledgers he weeps for his loss, but the fakir sits calmly by the same fire, because he has no records of debt and no hoard to lose. Please write a doha for that.
fire, moneylender, fakir
After the fire at the money-lender's office everyone ran to save what they could, and the old fakir across the road just sat and watched, completely at ease.
Fire takes the moneylender's ledger and the fakir's silence alike, but only the fakir smiles.
I have been living with just two sets of clothes for a year now, and I have never felt more free from worry.
What the fakir has not gathered, the world cannot steal, and what the fakir has not loved of the world, the world cannot take.
Please write a doha for a person who has decided to let go of most of their belongings, finds that they are more at ease, and sees that owning nothing is a kind of strength that no loss can touch.
fearless poverty chosen
doha about the fakir who has nothing to fear
The wheel is idle, the bridge is crossed, and the fakir walks on with nothing, for owning nothing weighs nothing.
My aunt gave away her spinning wheel and her small plot, crossed the bridge to the ashram, and told us she had never felt so light.
spinning wheel, bridge, fakir
doha with a spinning wheel and a bridge, about a fakir with nothing to lose
Write a doha where the fakir leaves his spinning wheel at the bank, crosses the bridge with empty hands, and walks into the town with no fear, because he has nothing that anyone could take from him.

I want a doha about the rare joy of the person who chose to live with almost nothing, who sleeps wherever he is, eats whatever he is given and fears neither theft nor loss nor the opinions of the rich.
doha for the free spirit who owns nothing
fakir, utterly free
A poor man's cloak with a king's heart: this is the fakir, owning nothing, fearing nothing, answerable to none.
A man at my gym quit his job, sold his flat, and now lives out of one small bag, and he has the calmest face I have seen.
The mountain asks nothing of the tree and the tree owns nothing of the mountain, and the fakir sits between, as free as both.
Write a doha where a fakir sits beneath a tree on a mountain, owning neither tree nor mountain nor so much as a blanket, and finds that this very absence of ownership frees him from every fear.
On our trek up the mountain we passed an old man sleeping under a tree with nothing but a cloth bag, and he looked like the freest soul alive.
doha with a mountain and a tree, about a fakir who owns nothing
mountain, tree, owning nothing
moon, fakir, fearless
The moon keeps no estate and counts no savings, and the fakir who sleeps beneath it with nothing to call his own shares in her freedom; please write a doha about this joy of owning nothing.
doha with the moon, about a fakir who has nothing to lose
One night I saw a homeless-looking holy man sleeping on the roadside under the full moon with the calmest face, and I envied him.
The moon is the fakir's companion and the fakir the moon's guest, and neither owns a single thing.
crossroads, fakir, free
At the crossroads the fakir stands with empty hands, for every road is his and none of them is owned.
Write a doha where a fakir reaches a crossroads and need not decide which road to take for gain, because he owns nothing and fears nothing, and every path is open to the free.
doha with a crossroads, about a fakir who owns nothing so he can go anywhere
I stood at a crossroads of my own life last year and gave up my job to do what I love, with almost no money, and for the first time I felt unafraid.

Please write a doha about a person who gave away the family property and now lives in a rented corner, owning nothing and wanting nothing, and who is happier than any of the relatives who quarrelled over the land.
chosen emptiness, fearless
Having nothing, the fakir has everything, for there is nothing between him and the open sky.
doha about giving away everything and being free
When my father signed the family land over to the village school he looked ten years younger.
The village physician, who earns almost nothing, once said the only man he could not worry about was the old fakir who rowed his boat across each morning with nothing to his name.
Write a doha where a physician and a fakir share a boat across the water, and the physician carries medicines and fears for them while the fakir owns nothing and fears nothing, free as the wind.
doha with a boat and a physician, about a fakir with nothing to lose
boat, physician, fakir
The physician guards his herbs in the boat, the fakir guards nothing, and the fakir alone crosses without fear.
bitter gourd, cleric, fakir
The cleric wears his garb of learning, the fakir only his freedom; one feasts, the other eats bitter gourd and is not afraid.
doha with a bitter gourd and a cleric, about a fakir who owns nothing
Write a doha where a cleric argues over property and rank while a fakir eats a plain bitter gourd under the open sky, owning nothing and fearing nothing, and is the happier of the two.
At the wedding the cleric argued about the fees, while the fakir at the entrance, who had nothing and asked for nothing, ate his bitter gourd curry quietly and left.
The heron stands on a stone with nothing and fears no hunter, and the fakir sits beside it, owning nothing, as free as the bird.
Walking along the lake I saw a heron on a stone, and an old mendicant sitting beside it with no bag at all, both of them equally unbothered.
doha with a heron and a stone, about a fakir with nothing to lose
stone, heron, owning nothing

Write a doha where a fakir sits on a stone beside a patient heron, both of them owning nothing and wanting nothing, and neither is troubled by any fear, since neither has anything that could be taken.
doha about how having nothing means youre totally free
nothing to lose
The fakir has locked nothing and counted nothing, and for that reason he alone is at ease in the world.
Please write a doha for the one who chooses to live without owning anything, finds that he has no fear of loss, and walks through the world as a guest who has already paid his debts.
A friend who sold his belongings and left on a long pilgrimage with just a backpack wrote that he has never been so unafraid of anything in his life.
churn, clay, fakir
My grandmother's churn and the potter's clay are the only things she kept when she gave everything else away, and she says she has never been so free from worry.
The churn is empty, the clay is dry, and the fakir who needs neither sleeps free of every fear.
doha with a churn and potter and clay, about a fakir with nothing
Write a doha where a fakir passes a woman at her churn and a potter at his clay, both of whom work to own more, and he blesses them, owning nothing, fearing nothing, and walks on.
Beside the oil press and the cremation ground the fakir sleeps with nothing, for the ground takes all alike and he has already given his all.
doha with an oil press and a cremation ground, about a fakir who owns nothing
Our colony fakir sleeps near the oil press and the cremation ground, owning nothing, and he is the only person I know who is not afraid of either.

Write a doha where a fakir sits between the oil press and the cremation ground, one grinding for gain and the other claiming all, and he alone is calm because he already owns nothing for either to take.
oil press, cremation ground, fakir
The boat carries the fakir across the water and he has nothing but a shroud's worth of cloth, and no fear of the far shore.
Aboard the ferry, the only passenger without luggage was an old man in a plain wrap that looked almost like a shroud, and he sat with perfect calm.

Write a doha where a fakir crosses water in a boat wearing something like a shroud, owning nothing more, and fearing neither storm nor shore, since he has already given up everything the water could take.
boat, shroud, fakir
doha with a boat and a shroud, about a fakir who owns nothing
Please write a doha about the fakir who is offered a bar of gold by a rich patron and gently refuses, saying that a man who owns nothing walks lighter than a man weighed down by even a little.
doha with gold, about a fakir who says no to riches
Someone once tried to give my uncle a gold chain for his kindness, and he returned it, saying a man with nothing is a man with no fear.
Gold shines before the fakir's eyes and he turns away, for he knows what the owner never learns: what is owned, owns.
gold refused, fearless
The old woman who sells swans of clay in our village eats only bitter gourd and rice, owns nothing beyond her room, and walks about with the calm of someone who has no fear at all.
doha with bitter gourd and a swan, about a fakir who has nothing
bitter gourd, swan, fakir
The swan owns the whole lake without a deed, the fakir eats bitter gourd without a care, and both are rich in being free.
Write a doha where a fakir shares his simple meal of bitter gourd beside a swan on the lake, owning nothing, fearing nothing, and finding that his emptiness is the greatest freedom a person can have.
A shroud has no pockets and a tree has no deed, and the fakir who knows this lives under the tree as if already in a shroud, owning nothing and fearing nothing. Please write a doha for this.
shroud, tree, fakir
Under the tree the fakir lies in his plain shroud-like cloth, and the world's keepers of property cannot reach him.
doha with a shroud and a tree, about the fakir who owns nothing
I met a quiet old man under a tree who had given everything away and now wore only a plain white wrap, and he told me he is afraid of nothing.
My teacher gave away his books, his home and his salary, and now moves from town to town, free as the wind, unafraid of what tomorrow will bring.
The fakir has nothing to shut, no seat to lose, no name to protect; he is what remains when nothing is held.
nothing owned, nothing feared
Please write a doha about the dignity of a person who chose to be without, whose freedom comes from having nothing to defend, and who is unafraid of what the world can do to him.
write a doha on the freedom of the wandering saint who owns nothing
The washerman scrubs the rich man's cloth, the chakor bird watches the night sky, and the fakir owns neither and is happier than both.
washerman, chakor bird, fakir
doha with a washerman and a chakor bird, about a fakir who owns nothing
Write a doha where a washerman works for a few coins and a chakor bird gazes at the sky with longing, while a fakir who owns nothing passes by free, fearless and contented in his emptiness.
A washerman in our lane told me that the fakir sleeping near his ghat is the only person in town who does not worry about money.

I would like a doha for those who have chosen to live without possessions, who find that nothing owned means nothing feared, and who walk through life with a peace the owners of the world can only envy.
free because empty-handed
With nothing in his hands, the fakir holds the whole world lightly; with nothing to lose, he cannot lose.
doha about the fakir who chose to own nothing
At my friend's minimalist home everything is gone except a mat and a cup, and she says she has never been so unafraid.
The rich man keeps a bird in a cage and fears for his home, while a fakir sleeps in the mosque courtyard owning nothing, caged by nothing, and afraid of nothing; please write a doha on the contrast.
The cage holds the bird, the mosque holds the prayer, and the fakir, who owns nothing, is held by no one.
doha with a mosque and a cage, about a fakir who owns nothing and is free
Outside the mosque a man sleeps on the steps with nothing and no fear, while the trader nearby keeps a hundred worries.
mosque, cage, fakir
ocean, fakir, fearless
At the beach I met an elderly man with no belongings who stared at the ocean without any concern at all and said, I own the same ocean you do.

Write a doha where a fakir stands before the ocean, owning nothing, wanting nothing, and fearing no wave, because a man who has given up all possession has nothing left that the ocean could ever take.
The ocean takes the rich man's ship and the fakir's silence is never touched, for he has nothing to lose to it.
doha with the ocean, about a fakir who has nothing and fears nothing
sword, snake, fakir
Our neighbour who guards his goods with a sword by the bed jumps at every sound, while the wandering fakir who sleeps outside, even near snakes, rests as calm as a baby.
The sword is for the owner and the snake for the careless, but the fakir owns nothing and is bitten by neither fear.
Write a doha where a fakir lies down beside a snake and a sword left by the road, owning nothing and fearing nothing, while those who own much tremble at every hint of loss.
doha with a sword and a snake, about the fakir who has nothing to fear
A drop of dew on the fakir's hand is all he owns, and it is more than enough to keep him free.
doha with dew, about a fakir who owns nothing, not even a bowl
I woke early at the monastery, saw the monk walking barefoot through the dew with no belongings, and felt a calm I'd never known.
Please write a doha where a fakir walks barefoot through the morning dew with empty hands, carrying nothing and fearing nothing, as light as the dew itself, and shows what it is to be free of owning.
dew, owning nothing
nothing lost, nothing feared
When my business collapsed I was devastated, but my grandmother, who gave up her holdings years ago, said she had never missed any of it and she looked at me with such peace.
doha for the fakir who owns nothing and so is free
To own nothing is to be owned by nothing, and to fear nothing is to be king of everything.

Please write a doha for the person who has realised that every possession is a worry, every title a fear, and who therefore chose to walk lightly, owning nothing, in a freedom no wealthy man has ever known.
On the old ferry boat the only passenger with no luggage was a thin fakir who sat beside a tortoise someone had caught, and he looked calmer than the wealthy merchants around him.
boat, tortoise, fakir
Write a doha where a fakir rides in a boat with a tortoise that carries its entire home on its back, while he carries nothing at all, owning nothing and free from every fear of loss.
The tortoise carries its home and the boat carries its load, but the fakir carries nothing and sails like the wind.
doha with a boat and a tortoise, about a fakir who owns nothing
doha with a chakor bird and a palace, about the fakir who owns nothing
chakor bird, palace, fakir
Outside the palace gates a chakor bird sang while a wandering saint who owned nothing walked right through the crowd without fear.
The palace owns a thousand rooms and the chakor owns its longing for the sky, but the fakir owns nothing, and no one can threaten him.
Write a doha where a fakir walks through the gates of a great palace, while a chakor bird looks on, and the fakir, owning nothing, fears no guard, no king, and no loss, and is the freest soul there.
doha with philosopher's stone and a needle, about the fakir who owns nothing
philosopher's stone, needle, fakir
A friend of mine hunted for an investment that would turn everything into riches, while his grandmother, who owns one needle and one cloth, laughed at him for fearing loss.

Write a doha where the fakir is offered a philosopher's stone and a needle of silver but declines both, saying that owning nothing frees him from every fear of loss, and that this is the greatest alchemy.
Let the philosopher's stone be turned to wealth, the fakir needs only a needle to mend his single cloth.
Write a doha where a yogi in a cotton wrap sits with his hands empty, owning nothing but the breath he breathes, and finds that this very poverty is the greatest freedom a man can know.
Cotton on the body and nothing in the hand, the yogi sits fearless, for there is no one who can take from him.
yogi, cotton, owning nothing
doha with a yogi and cotton, about someone who owns nothing and fears nothing
A yogi who lives by our village wears one cotton cloth, owns nothing, and when floods came he was the only one not scrambling to save things.
stars, sandalwood, fakir
doha with stars and sandalwood, about a fakir who owns nothing
Write a doha where a fakir lies beneath the stars with a piece of sandalwood as his only comfort, owning nothing, wanting nothing, and fearing nothing, as free as any ruler of the earth.
Camping under the stars, a stranger offered us a piece of sandalwood and said it was the only thing he owned, and he seemed the richest man in the camp.
The stars are the fakir's ceiling and sandalwood his only scent; he owns nothing and fears nothing under heaven.
doha with a musk deer and an oil press, about a fakir who owns nothing
musk deer, oil press, fakir
The musk deer carries its scent unknowing, the oil press grinds out another's gain, and the fakir wanders free of both.
Write a doha where a musk deer wanders unaware of the treasure it carries, and an oil press grinds all day for profit, while a fakir passes by, owning nothing and fearing no loss of anything.
In the village the oil press runs from dawn to dusk for the owner's gain, while the wandering fakir sits in the shade, has no worry, and smiles at everyone.
milk, palanquin, fakir
doha with milk and a palanquin, about a fakir who owns nothing
A rich man rides in a palanquin and drinks milk from a silver cup, fearing for his comfort, while a fakir walks on foot with empty hands, afraid of nothing; please write a doha for this contrast.
The palanquin sways with its fearful passenger and the fakir walks beside it, sipping a little milk and owning nothing.
At my cousin's wedding the groom came in a palanquin worried about every detail, while the old fakir at the gate, sipping a cup of milk, looked happier than anyone.
doha with a forest, about a fakir who owns nothing
forest, fakir, free
Write a doha where a fakir walks into the forest with empty hands and no plan, fearing neither animal nor weather, since he owns nothing that either could take, and finds his freedom in that.
In the forest the fakir owns no branch and fears no ghost, for what is not owned cannot be lost.
My uncle left city life to live in a forest hut with nothing but what he could carry, and he writes that he has never felt less afraid.
